status: No concrete issue found in bounded read-only presenter integration review.
scope: Read source and three presenter diffs against sealed core API and ledger. No code edits, test/build execution, browser/desktop or GPU runs. Existing core/probe outcome reports were not re-audited.
checked: live_bytes includes retained native charge beside active bundle/readback, packet capacities, scratch and benchmark reservation, preserving the next-UI 16 MiB allowance and existing 128 MiB limit. Native reserve/checkout preflight 16 MiB bundle, 24 MiB bundle+readback, checked current aggregate and acquired/deadline/stop state before atomic charge changes.

Only one owner-held retired slot exists. Exact core context/key/descriptor compatibility is checked before checkout. Miss/CPU upload/reconfigure evicts outside the mutex, with handle destruction/drop preceding retained-charge acknowledgment and replacement allocation. Acquire-none does not check out a compatible cache.

Allocation returns the complete lease before queue writes. The lease remains outside the fallible encode closure. MayHaveWrites precedes encoding; incomplete encoders are dropped, metadata is flushed at most once, and the specific submission is polled under the existing deadline. Every reverse error scope is collected, including after earlier failures.

Cache admission additionally requires successful complete draws, known retirement, successful scopes/readback, presentation and requested verification, no cancellation/suboptimal result, and a final under-lock current/stop/failure/deadline check. Core marking precedes transfer; only an infallible Option move follows successful charge transfer. Declined transfers keep active charge until safely dropped/idle or owner release.

Uncertain retirement uses ordinary handle drop and owner failure/release, never explicit destroy or recache. Readback is not retained. idle preserves retired charge; begin_release does not clear it. Only outer acknowledgment after run_owner and Gpu/lease drops clears retained charge. Driver callback failure cannot manufacture reuse or release.

Existing timing phase calls and successful completion ordering are preserved: packet drops before idle; active/readback charges must be zero before completion, separately retained cache is allowed, and reports still require positive owner release. Cache-return work remains within owner-total/prepare-through-present durations even when outside the individual cleanup bracket. Native cache stores no Plan, CPU reference, scene identity or stamp.

Inspected ten new synthetic groups: seven ledger/accounting/deadline/timing groups and three eviction-order/failure/empty-slot groups. Their assertions exercise charge transfer, exact limits, stop/stale refusal, post-drop acknowledgment and positive release; no claim that these pure tests inject real driver failures.
limitations: Explicit buffer accounting preserves existing driver, queue staging, pipeline/bind-group and allocator-overhead exclusions; synchronous driver-call interruption remains outside the guarantee. Completion is an owner proof supplied to the core lease API, not something the lease independently detects.
